tagline.text: A resort complex with three hotels, a casino and DreamPlay

location.label: Location
location.text: Corner of Asean Avenue and Roxas Boulevard, Entertainment City, Parañaque

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (indoor-focused, so possible year-round)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱350~3,000 (per person per day, including admission and meals, estimated)

children.text: City of Dreams Manila is an integrated resort of about 6.2 hectares in Entertainment City on the Manila Bay side. Three hotels, a casino, the family indoor play center DreamPlay, and a shopping and dining strip sit in one place, which suits rainy days and relaxing, resort-style itineraries.

City of Dreams Manila is an integrated resort in Entertainment City in Barangay Tambo, Parañaque. It stands at the corner where Asean Avenue meets Roxas Boulevard, on a site of about 6.2 hectares (15 acres). It is operated by Melco Resorts, which also runs a resort of the same name in Macau, and it had a soft opening in December 2014 before its grand opening in February 2015. In Entertainment City it was the second resort to open, after Solaire.

The complex has three hotels, Hyatt Regency Manila, Nobu Hotel Manila and Nüwa Manila (formerly Crown Towers), with about 940 rooms combined. Besides the hotels there are a casino, the dome-shaped Fortune Egg, a shopping strip called The Shops at The Boulevard, and the family indoor play space DreamPlay. Because lodging, dining and play are all handled within one cluster of buildings, it is a good fit for days when you do not want to travel far from where you are staying in Manila.

There are roughly three reasons to visit. The first is a relaxing stay built around the hotels and restaurants, the second is an outing to DreamPlay with children, and the third is the casino and nightlife. It is not a place to go for historic sites in the city center or for beaches, so it is best to keep it separate from history-focused days at places like Intramuros or Rizal Park. Here is a simple way to plan a first visit. With children, a half-day plan built around DreamPlay with lunch and dinner inside the resort is the easiest. For adults, staying one night with dinner and evening entertainment as the focus means less travel. It is also a good choice when you need a full day of rest in Manila, or when you want to stay close to the airport the night before departure. On the other hand, if you want to see as many sights as possible during a short stay in Manila, limit this place to a single dinner.

Getting here is much easier than it used to be. In November 2024 the first phase of the LRT-1 Cavite Extension opened, adding the MIA Road and Redemptorist–Aseana stations along Roxas Boulevard. However, no confirmed source describes the walk from the station to the resort entrance, so check a map app, and in the heat of the day consider taking Grab for the last stretch.

Hyatt Regency Manila is a five-star hotel of about 360 rooms, and Nobu Hotel Manila is known as the first Nobu hotel in Asia, with Robert De Niro among its backers. Nüwa Manila, the former Crown Towers, is the most upscale room line. Room counts differ slightly between sources, so treat it as roughly 940 rooms.

A family indoor play space themed on DreamWorks Animation characters, located on the upper floor of The Shops at The Boulevard. About eleven zones operate, including a Shrek swamp stomp, dragon-flying slides, wall climbing, a cooking experience and a 4D theater. Participants must be at least
80 cm

tall, and some attractions have separate height and weight limits. Guardians can enter on a non-participating ticket to watch, and children under 10 are reported to need a guardian with them. Outside food is restricted, so have snacks in the shopping area beforehand.

An American-style casino reported to have about 290 gaming tables and about 1,600 slot machines. Philippine rules require ID and age verification for entry, so bring your passport, and check the latest notice for dress and entry conditions before you visit.

blocks.title: Fortune Egg and The Shops at The Boulevard

children.text: The Fortune Egg is the complex's signature dome-shaped building, a space for shows and events. The Shops at The Boulevard is a connected strip of restaurants and shops with Japanese, Chinese, Italian, Thai and Korean options for a light meal, which makes it good for walking around on a rainy day.

Crystal Dragon is a Cantonese and regional Chinese restaurant on the Nüwa Manila side, and Nobu Manila is the flagship Japanese fusion restaurant. Outdoor-terrace spots such as Wave and Breezes have also been featured at the Nobu hotel. Menus and hours change often, so confirm before booking. For groups or celebrations, it is better to ask in advance about seating and set menus.

Haliya and The Café regularly appear in holiday-menu news as signature restaurants. The Café at Hyatt Regency is known for its buffet, which is comfortable for families with children. Special buffets are often held at year-end and on holidays.

Entertainment City is a gaming and leisure zone of about 8 square kilometers west of Roxas Boulevard and south of the SM Mall of Asia complex. Solaire and Okada Manila are in the same district, so it is also a good place to compare resorts, and it is close to Manila Bay's sunset spots.
Arrive at the resort and have lunch at The Shops at The Boulevard. Check DreamPlay's operating days and hours beforehand by phone or official channel.
Enter DreamPlay. Have children wear sneakers, socks and a shirt with sleeves, and use the lockers for bags.

The next morning, have the breakfast buffet, check out and head to the airport.

Because the facilities are mainly indoors, you can visit year-round. If you will be walking outdoors, the dry season from November to May is more comfortable.
In the rainy season from June to October showers are frequent, but it is a good time to spend in the shops and hotels. During typhoon season, however, leave room in your travel plans.

For lodging, choose among Hyatt Regency Manila, Nobu Hotel Manila and Nüwa Manila. Hyatt suits family trips, Nobu suits those who want a stylish atmosphere, and Nüwa suits those who want the most upscale room line. Prices vary greatly by date and events, so compare booking sites with the hotels' official channels.

For food, the main choices are Crystal Dragon's Cantonese cooking, Nobu Manila's Japanese fusion, and the buffets and specials at Haliya and The Café. The Shops at The Boulevard has light restaurants serving Italian, Thai, Korean and more. There is competition for year-end specials and bookings, so reserve early.

You do not have to be a hotel guest to use most of the restaurants. However, waits get long at busy times, so book dinner by phone or online. With children, the Hyatt Regency buffet or the light restaurants in the shops are less of a burden, and for adult gatherings the signature Japanese and Chinese restaurants have a nicer atmosphere. SM Mall of Asia nearby also has many options, so having one meal there depending on your plans is another option.

As of 2026 DreamPlay is reported to run Wednesday to Sunday, 11:00-20:00 (last entry about 19:00), and to be closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. Some dates have opened late, so confirm by phone or official channel before you visit.
DreamPlay participants must wear sneakers, socks and a shirt with sleeves, and slippers are not allowed in.

Parking may be free only after validation at the guest desk, so keep your receipt.
The shops are good for half a day on a rainy day, but choose your travel time to avoid rush-hour traffic on Roxas Boulevard.
You can combine nearby Solaire and Okada Manila to see Entertainment City in one day.
Rooms and restaurants fill up quickly at year-end and on weekends, so book early.
If you stay the night before a flight, set your airport transfer time early and book a Grab in advance to avoid morning rush-hour traffic.
Pool and facility access conditions differ by room class and date, so confirm at check-in.
Casinos carry a risk of gambling addiction, so set a budget limit before you play. Check the latest notice for age limits and entry conditions.
Avoid casino money-changers and private currency exchange offers, and use only official counters.

Watch your smartphone and wallet, and do not leave bags unattended in crowded places.
